_note: Core/Net (parity/F05-net.md), the CLASSIFICATION fold: a raw platform path snapshot in, the five reported facts out. Kept pure so all three renderers can be judged by the same cases; the platform reads that feed it (NWPath, NetworkCapabilities, navigator.connection) are per-renderer plumbing and are not pinned here. THE RULES THIS PINS: (1) VPN wins over the transport underneath, because a tunnel rides on top of wifi or cellular and reporting the carrier would hide the thing the app asked about; (2) an unsatisfied path is `none` and nothing else is inspected; (3) `expensive` is the METERED flag, never `type == cellular` (a personal hotspot over wifi is metered, and unlimited cellular is not); (4) `constrained` is the user's data-saving setting and is independent of everything else; (5) `online` is `reachable` AND the last probe verdict, which is the entire reason the two fields exist separately (an interface can be up while a captive portal eats every request); (6) `generation` is empty unless the link is cellular AND the platform volunteered the radio family without a permission prompt.
_runner: Runners: TS (@despia/kernel net-core.ts, packages/kernel/test/net-conformance.test.ts), Kotlin (:core NetCore/NetDebounce, NetConformanceTest), Swift (Engine/iOS/NetCore.swift, NetConformance in the record lane). All three read THIS file, and Core/Net calls the same core rather than a parallel copy.

classify.name: a personal hotspot is wifi AND metered, which is why expensive is not a type test
unlimited cellular is cellular and NOT expensive
a tunnel over wifi reports vpn, not wifi
a tunnel over cellular still reports vpn, and stays metered
a transport nobody named is other, never a guess
an unsatisfied path is none and nothing else is inspected
data saving is independent of the link

online.name: reachable with no probe yet is online
reachable with a failed probe is OFFLINE, which is the captive-portal case
unreachable is offline whatever the probe said

generation.name: lte on a cellular link is 4g
a radio family on a wifi link is not reported
a withheld radio family is empty, never a guess

probe._note: The reachability verdict from one completed request. Redirects are never followed, so the response IS the 3xx and its Location is readable: a redirect to ANOTHER host is the captive-portal signature, while a same-host redirect (an http to https upgrade) is a normal, reachable answer.

cases.name: a cross-host redirect is a captive portal
a redirect with no Location is not reachable
404 reached a server but not the app
a dead transport resolves rather than throwing
